    Arrows of an admissible presentation are independent modulo R² #

    Since the kernel of an admissible presentation lies in the square of the arrow ideal, the images of the arrows are linearly independent modulo paths of length at least two (arrInd). For each arrow a, a two-dimensional representation of kQ in which only a acts nonzero and all words of length two vanish detects the coefficient of a.

    source
    theorem BrickAccessibility.Statement.AdmissiblePresentation.exists_arrow_rep {k : Type u} [Field k] {Λ : Type u} [Ring Λ] [Algebra k Λ] (P : AdmissiblePresentation k Λ) (a : P.Q.A) :
    ∃ (φ : FinQuiver.PathAlgebra k P.Q →ₐ[k] Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) k), (∀ (l : List P.Q.A), 2 ≤ l.length → φ (FinQuiver.word k P.Q l) = 0) ∧ ∀ (b : P.Q.A), φ (FinQuiver.arrow k P.Q b) = !![0, if b = a then 1 else 0; 0, 0]

    theorem BrickAccessibility.Statement.AdmissiblePresentation.stringQuotient_exact {k : Type u} [Field k] {Λ : Type u} [Ring Λ] [Algebra k Λ] (P : AdmissiblePresentation k Λ) [FiniteDimensional k Λ] (hP : P.IsSpecialBiserial) :
    ∃ (x : P.toPathData.socIdeal.IsTwoSided) (D' : MonomialData k (Λᵐᵒᵖ ⧸ P.toPathData.socIdeal)), D'.IsStringAlgebra ∧ ∀ (M : Type u) [inst : AddCommGroup M] [inst_1 : Module Λᵐᵒᵖ M] [inst_2 : Module k M] [IsScalarTower k Λᵐᵒᵖ M] [FiniteDimensional k M], IsIndecomposable Λᵐᵒᵖ M → ¬Module.IsTorsionBySet Λᵐᵒᵖ M ↑P.toPathData.socIdeal → Module.Projective Λᵐᵒᵖ M ∧ Module.Injective Λᵐᵒᵖ M ∧ ¬IsUniserialMod Λᵐᵒᵖ M

    Lemma 5.3 for Λ = kQ/I special biserial: with J the sum of the socles of the nonuniserial injective summands e_iΛ (right modules, as left Λᵐᵒᵖ-modules), J is a two-sided ideal, Λ/J is a string algebra, and every indecomposable right module not annihilated by J is a nonuniserial projective-injective module.
